### NODE-0830 · Keep ambient string transitions continuous across notes and the loop

**2026-11-21 · Changed · Implemented · Local**

Remove the cello’s phrase gaps, overlap instrument changes evenly and carry the same F regions through the one-minute loop boundary.

- The user reported that the transition did not feel good. The prior cello envelope lasted 6.4 seconds at 7.5-second starts, leaving about 1.1 seconds before each new attack. Replace isolated fade-out/restarts with 2.4-second cello and 2.8-second bass equal-power handoffs. Retain the same eight/twelve score positions and F-major pitches.
- Merge adjacent identical pitches, including the closing and opening F, into seven cello and six bass regions. Sustain those tones with crossfaded recorded-body loops and periodic filter/room state. Both instrument envelope powers remain one throughout the period; the F regions continue through sixty seconds rather than retriggering at zero. The source recordings and string-only rule remain unchanged.
- Match the previous quiet average level at approximately -34.4 dBFS RMS. Rebuild WAV, score, manifest, native player and exact end/start excerpt; add fresh legato.html and quiet-workshop-ambient-legato-60s.wav routes. Update current plan, system, author guide and style references. This refines the handoffs from NODE-0828 without changing the selected ambient/no-piano direction.

Topics: Audio · Interface · Testing · Documentation

### NODE-0827 · Soften the flowing melody on cello and double bass

**2026-11-21 · Changed · Implemented · Local**

Address the cello’s harsh tone and the request to try bass too with gentler, volume-matched renders of the same flowing one-minute melody on both instruments.

- Retain the 57-note F2–F3 F-major variation, sixteen bars and 64 BPM. Start 350 ms into each recorded sustain to avoid the initial bow transient, use 220 ms attacks and 420 ms releases, reduce upper-mid resonance and apply a two-pole low-pass at 1.6 kHz for cello / 1.8 kHz for bass. Both renders target -28 dBFS RMS and preserve circular note/reflection tails. No clipping, hard limiting or new sample download.
- Reuse the CC0 recorded cello and solo-contrabass banks. Add --soft and --soft --bass modes, separate players/WAVs/MIDI/scores/join excerpts and offline npm scripts. Both instruments play identical musical events; the softened bass now plays the flowing variation rather than the earlier low melody. The existing twenty-one bass/cello/lighter-cello deliverables remain byte-identical.
- Update current plan/system/style/author references and retain earlier versions for comparison. The normalized 2 kHz high-pass energy proxy decreases on soft cello, supporting a measured brightness reduction without asserting subjective comfort. User audition remains pending; no action-cue changes, campaign integration or publication.

<a id="node-0801"></a>
### NODE-0801 · Profile bounded undo retention and save recovery on archived factories

**2026-11-21 · Review · Recorded · Not applicable**

Measured current checkpoint memory and browser save costs before choosing an undo redesign; current gameplay and fifty-entry history remain unchanged.

- The user chose profiling before a memory-budget or selective-history redesign. Three factory sizes were measured: a fresh current-rule seed and current-normalized copies of archived 469-node/31-map and 1,159-node/64-map headless playtest layouts. The legacy archives do not establish current-rule balance or universal capacity.
- Three fresh Node processes per case retained about 3.11, 19.44 and 45.64 MiB above the no-history engine baseline at fifty checkpoints. Retention remained flat at seventy-five commands, oldest entries were evicted, snapshots were independent, fifty undos consumed the history and replacement cleared it. After undo, retained deltas fell to roughly 0.17/0.53/1.04 MiB, including the restored current state.
- Three Chromium trials per case measured actual writers without mounted App subscribers. Late-factory checkpoint medians were 2.6–2.7 ms, autosave 4.6–4.9 ms and manual save with three populated slots 26.2–28.3 ms; worst trial manual-save p95 was 43.1 ms. Measurements do not attribute manual cost among clone, collection serialization and returned-view normalization.
- An empty dedicated localhost origin reached native storage quota at 5,242,880 key/value code units. Failed growing autosave/manual writes preserved the earlier stored strings. Portable serialization/parse recovered current memory while full; removing disposable filler allowed Retry to clear failure and a manual save to succeed. All audit storage was cleaned.
- Recommendation for the next user review: retain current undo and defer a byte-budget or representation redesign; profile manual-save phases if latency work is chosen. This recommendation is not an accepted redesign decision. No code refactor, supported benchmark revival, factory-size guarantee or publication.

Topics: Performance · Saves · Documentation

Verification: Nine isolated Node workers and nine browser trials completed their checkpoint and persistence assertions. Browser native QuotaExceededError, prior-save preservation, export parse, retry/manual recovery and empty final storage passed; captured warning/error logs were empty after the corrected harness reload. SHA-256 checks preserved all 377 captured runtime source files and both original archive snapshots. Node heap is not browser/process memory. Desktop-only source harness, no renderer/subscriber load, no current-rule campaign or mod capacity claim, no actual file download UI. Game runtime unchanged; no new full-suite/build/publication needed. Six catalog freshness checks, local links across forty system documents and all six generated-history tests passed.

### NODE-0708 · Measure a practical 30 FPS zoom with restored node details

**2026-11-20 · Added · Implemented · Local**

Add exact starting zoom/detail options to the active-factory preview and measure a practical view with margin over 30 FPS.

- Support details=1 and zoom=0.25 for precise initial comparison views. Accept zoom requests from 0.05 to 2, preserve the starting zoom on Reset test, and expose actual clamped camera values in activity metadata. Fit all and Inspect a cell keep ordinary framing.
- Sweep 20/25/30/35/40 percent in the same built 2,400-node fixture with text and live boxes restored. Use five seconds of warmup and 25 seconds per sample, keeping production and cargo active across all nodes. Repeat 35 percent at the center and on the right side.
- At 35 percent, three runs averaged 59.16–76.24 FPS with frame p95 25.0–25.2 ms. At 30 percent, the average was 46.84 FPS with 33.4 ms p95. At 25 percent, the average was 31.08 FPS with 58.3 ms p95. Recommend 35 percent as a local practical setting, with occasional slower frames still possible.
- At 40 percent, overview caches are disabled and vector detail returns: average 33.48 FPS and p95 41.8 ms. This explains why a slightly closer view can be slower. Normal game detail rules and the live site remain unchanged.

Topics: Performance · Controls · Tooling · Documentation

Verification: Preview TypeScript, standalone build and two benchmark checks passed. Seven complete 25-second samples used the same 1,210 by 923 CSS pixel viewport and frozen build. Metadata confirmed actual zoom, visible-node counts, cache mode and continuing production, cargo and delivery. The 35 percent repeat moved from centered x=-1265.4 to right-side x=-2475.400044382537, with 433–444 visible nodes and all 2,400 still simulating. No new warning/error logs at final check. No full-suite-pass claim or universal 30 FPS floor: host load varied and frame p99 sometimes exceeded 33.3 ms. No simulation, campaign-save or live publication changes.

<a id="node-0659"></a>
### NODE-0659 · Add shared-border terrain and permanent Road crossing research to new worlds

**2026-11-20 · Added · Implemented · Published by 7c4abe4**

Implement rivers, mountains and chasms using the approved field artwork and Node Map presentation, with tiered worldwide crossing permission and clear-route safeguards.

- New standard worlds save sixteen river, twelve mountain and eight chasm shared edges under independent border layout version one. Whole-border placement blocks apply from either side; mixed terrain cannot form an adjacent-side right angle. Existing worlds normalize to clear version zero, including future discoveries.
- River Bridges at Hydro, Mountain Tunnels at Shiny and Chasm Spans at Complex each cost five of every Core through their tier and require Road plus the corresponding Core project. Normal Research Center payment grants independent worldwide permission. Players still build ordinary Road pairs with normal channels, clearance and shipment behavior; terrain remains with no separate after-research artwork.
- Seeded bounded generation preserves all Home edges, the E1–E2 lake corridor, two clear neighbors per map, a clear Manhattan shortest route from Home to every destination and a three-hop local bypass for every blocked edge. Larger grids scale quotas/ranges before first non-Home generation; existing layout versions and undo are preserved. Invalid layouts and unresearched saved paired crossings are rejected; factory templates exclude paired-sector nodes.
- Pixi reuses the approved vectors with matching clipped halves, canonical orientation and fixed width during field expansion. Only the selected Road placement/move ghost reveals the adjacent half. The main Node Map shows discovered waves, peaks and fracture marks and side/terrain rows without research requirement text, retaining symbols after research. Invalid held Road previews name the required project and highest Core tier, with a wrapped 12 CSS px warning kept inside the current field at overview zoom.
- Add a self-contained actual-engine test screen with synthetic empty fields and explicit research grants, keeping browser saves and minimap layout preferences untouched. Retain the art gallery and nine-sample modal reference. Update current map, Road, research, save, mod, interface, controls and testing references, the existing plan, generated catalogs and both Word references.
- The 1,100-world static audit reaches exact quotas with no fallback and at least three quadrants per type. Standard layouts touch 59–70 maps, exceeding the proposed 45–60 estimate while retaining agreed density and safeguards. Normal-play purchase timing, useful crossing frequency and progression-time balance remain pending; this is not a balance run.

Topics: World · Logistics · Research · Interface · Art · Saves · Documentation · Testing

Verification: Current src/scripts/previews suite passes 1,143 tests across 108 files, with one optional test/file skipped; archived release copies are excluded. Final save/mod/Road/terrain regression passes 173 tests after cleanup; renderer/Road/permission feedback checks pass 167 tests. Normal Research Center payment, independent projects, both-side atomic rejection, ghosts, reversal, extra channels, movement, copy/templates, undo, reload/imports, legacy worlds and grid resizing are covered. Audit checks 1,000 standard seeds and twenty for each of five larger grids: exact quotas, no fallback, all graph/corner safeguards pass. Browser verifies all terrain types blocked and researched, matching halves in all four directions, 36 map markers, side-only summaries, no research text in marker labels, desktop and 390 px layout without overflow, and no error logs. Repeated preview resets emitted four Pixi texture-source/sampler binding disposal warnings; rendering continued and the library nulls the destroyed bindings. Main and /node/ builds, preview types/build, six catalog generation/freshness/link checks and history checks pass. Both Word files preserve tables/unrelated text and reopen; packaged rendering fails because LibreOffice soffice.exe is absent, leaving Word page layout unverified. No normal-play balance run, player-save edit, commit or publication.

The revised proposal totals 72 ranks: six Simple-start chains, three Automata-start chains, three Hydro-start chains and one Shiny-start chain. Node discovery unlocks remain unchanged.
- Review revision: Extractor, Kiln and Smelter efficiency start at Basic Core with six ranks; Refiner and Assembler start at Automata Core with five; Tree Planter starts at Hydro Core with four. Other settled tiers remain unchanged. Update the proposal rules, examples and total to 64 upgrades, comprising 57 Production upgrades and seven Research Center upgrades. All recipes running in a Recycler, including Crust Recovery, use only Recycler upgrades at 85/65/50/35% base time from Hydro through Final. **2026-11-16 · Review · Recorded · Not applicable**

<a id="node-0529"></a>
### NODE-0529 · Propose one Bot Plant assembly time at each efficiency rank

**2026-11-16 · Decision · Superseded · Not applicable**

All frame and gun pairings would share one cycle time at a given efficiency rank. The curve starts at 75 seconds and removes 10% of the base cycle at each of six ranks from Simple through Complex, reaching 30 seconds. The ranks use standard machine research prices.

- The proposal also names the starter parts Basic Frame and Basic Gun in player-facing text.
- The component production target counts the whole chain for one continuously supplied Bot Plant at base and full research. The timing trial compared stronger upstream research and double-output part recipes for the tier being assembled. Both variants reduced the modeled Final chain from 228 to 124 production nodes.
- The proposal now follows the timing-only option. It lists base and researched cycles for all ten standard parts and whole-chain counts for all five matched tiers. Upstream processing and solid extraction reach 20% of base time at full research.
- The Goblin progression target uses one continuously supplied Bot Plant. A Camp should be sustainable with unresearched Basic bots. Villages and Kingdoms should require stronger parts and efficiency. Trial base cycles of 20, 32, and 55 seconds meet these targets with existing Goblin upkeep. The choice between tiered and shared assembly is open.

Topics: Production · Recipes · Research · Balance

Replaced by: [NODE-0530](<2026-11.md#node-0530>)

Verification: Checked the saved proposal against the current recipe timings and machine efficiency formula. Expanded standard recipe inputs recursively for all five matched pairs, pooled shared workloads, and rounded to whole production nodes. The capacity model assumes an adequately supplied factory and an unlocked Mythril reserve.

### NODE-0312 · Create, apply and share data mods through guided factory editors

**2026-11-04 · Added · Implemented · Published by eca1c2d**

Options now opens a Mods modal with category editors, base-game templates, local drafts, a change review, save-aware activation and copy/paste NODEMOD1 share codes.

- Guided forms edit existing resources/items, Production nodes including Extractors and Lake Intakes, Logistics/storage including Carts, world obstructions, research, recipes, map fields/reserves and connection/construction timings. Ingredients, yields, chance products, allowed recipes, socket types/counts/sharing, buffers and per-node cable limits are editable without JSON.
- Share codes encode versioned UTF-8 data with a copy-damage checksum. Strict validation rejects unsupported keys, invalid references and quantities, malformed codes and research dependency cycles before applying any changes. Scripts and new runtime behavior are outside the data format.
- Applied packages travel with saves and undo. Catalog activation retains cached research/build references and source-owned base templates; tutorials and clean factories use base rules. Playfield scenes refresh when a package changes. Active stock remains intact when capacities fall, and Cart total-capacity behavior remains enforced.
- Application and removal reject incompatible attached cables atomically. Reserve settings affect newly generated nodes/maps; build and travel settings affect future construction/shipments. Removing a package restores rules without rewinding stock, research or generated maps. Existing milestone triggers, scripted effects/caps and routing roles remain.
- A separate local paused factory verified Options to Mods, a named Wood-to-Timber draft, review/application, generated-code copy/reimport, damaged-code feedback, base-template recovery after development updates and Production-editor controls. No existing browser factory or save was used for these edits.

Topics: Mods · Interface · Production · Logistics · Connections · Recipes · Research · World generation · Persistence · Documentation

Verification: 19 focused mod tests pass. Full Vitest run: 699 passed, one pre-existing skip; TypeScript/Vite production build passes with the existing large-bundle warning. Browser interaction checked at http://127.0.0.1:4180/ in the default 1280 by 720 viewport. No full balance run, cross-device browser certification or publication.

### NODE-0232 · Show Road flow arrows and move cargo directly without Road storage

**2026-11-03 · Changed · Superseded · Local**

Roads show a large flow arrow, use standard header icons and hold no inventory. Map Road hovers show only direction and item; Cart-family nodes use an icon header and the same shading dimensions as Roads.

- A large filled arrow below the Road header points toward the map edge for export and into the field for import. It derives orientation from the inward-facing socket, supports all four faces, appears in placement previews and updates when pair direction changes. Header symbols match the standard 21-unit node icon in a 33-unit plate.
- Cart, Truck, Train and legacy Chest visuals replace header title text with the existing centered storage icon. Their 42-unit shaded header matches Road geometry. Keep the four-by-five capacity squares, 128-unit footprint, inventory capacities, ports, serialized IDs and control-group markers.
- Minimap and expanded-map Road tooltips contain only a compass route such as H to W1 and the material name. Infer material from both ends, wiring and stock, with the last assigned cable item as a fallback when empty. Remove the Road transport label and verbose map names.
- Each export check moves one item directly from a connected upstream inventory to a connected downstream input, at 12 items per minute. Support local logistics routes on both sides, exact recipe sockets, shared or per-item capacity, real in-flight reservations, single-material and fluid restrictions, valid reciprocal roles, and Dev Source. No receiving or sending Road inventory is filled. Disconnected/full destinations leave cargo at its source, and missed trips never accumulate.
- Local cable animation uses cosmetic pulses and never reserves receiving inventory. Existing save cargo returns to connected inventories if space permits; any remainder is preserved in the shared pool. Pending Road deliveries refund their original sources before migration. Migration clears Road bags, sets capacity to zero and is idempotent; retired Fluid Road cargo retains its prior compatibility handling.
- Retain atomic paired placement, face-slot rules and one-way direction controls from NODE-0228. Direction changes still disconnect endpoint cables for rewiring; stock remains in actual inventories. Expansion dialogue and checks now wait for both Carts to be connected before shipping, rather than treating a Road endpoint as storage.
- NODE-0433 replaces sending-side routing and direct non-vehicle feeds. Road graphics, cargo recovery, and receiving-side routing remain in use.

### NODE-0228 · Validate facing Road pairs and toggle one-way flow from either endpoint

**2026-11-03 · Changed · Superseded · Local**

Roads create facing endpoints together only when both placements are legal. Clicking either endpoint opens a compact Road flow panel: click its direction card to reverse the pair, with 5 sec / item underneath.

- Retain atomic validation of both locations and both face-slot limits. Select the nearest intended map face first; if its neighbor is locked, reject placement instead of snapping to a different unlocked face. Valid pairs have reciprocal IDs, facing edges and opposite sending/receiving roles.
- Road clicks and configuration controls open the side panel. Its only content below the title is the clickable direction card and 5 sec / item, per the follow-up request; explanatory subtext, separate Send/Receive cards, material summaries and other text are removed.
- An explicit setRoadDirection operation updates both endpoints to complementary roles; reverseRoad delegates to it. An already-selected direction is a no-op. Reversing preserves stored items and disconnects both endpoint cable sets for rewiring, retaining existing direction-change behavior. No new face slots are used.
- Only export-to-import pairs dispatch across maps. Malformed double-export or mismatched counterpart references cannot dispatch; valid explicit direction selection can repair complementary roles. Legacy omitted reverse references remain compatible.
- Expansion copy explains paired legal placement and one-way flow. Its direction toggle is disabled during practice to preserve the required lesson route; normal play permits reversal from either endpoint.

Topics: Roads · Logistics · Interface · Tutorials · Testing

Browser QA at port 4175 in a separate paused factory used Dev research/map unlocks, placed a Road and visited its automatically created counterpart, verified opposite roles and control from each map, then rebuilt/reloaded and verified the final single card toggles H to E1 and E1 to H while only 5 sec / item remains below. ### NODE-0225 · Add Road-unlocked Carts, global Truck and Train upgrades, and shared face slots

**2026-11-03 · Changed · Implemented · Local**

Wooden Chests become Road-unlocked Carts. Sequential Trucks and Trains research upgrades every vehicle to 40 and 80 items without replacement; all solid tiers are allowed from the start. Road faces support one, then two, then three endpoints through sequential upgrades.

- Retain serialized woodenChest/chest node kinds, IDs, wiring, stock, geometry and the existing two-second local output cycle. Normal new placement and copies require Road research; existing vehicles remain usable. Generated saved names and templates update to Cart, Truck or Train, with player-authored titles retained. Build, shortcuts and placement text use the current vehicle name.
- Use capacities of 20 for Cart, 40 for Truck and 80 for Train, shared across input/output stock and pending input reservations. Preserve saved over-capacity stock rather than deleting it; the existing four-by-five block display shows the filled proportion.
- Trucks costs 20 each Simple, Basic and Automata Cores after Road and Automata Core. Trains costs 40 each through Hydro after Trucks and Hydraulic Assembly. Completion upgrades all existing sector nodes and saved templates in place, and future placements start at the current level. Load, state replacement, developer research unlocks and undo reconcile the same level.
- The user explicitly rejected material-tier restrictions: every solid product and Core tier is allowed in the first Cart. New fluid inputs, including Water, Coolant and Conductive Slurry, are blocked in every vehicle level, including routed/legacy connections and Dev Source supply. Existing stored material is preserved.
- Road Channels 1 retains its 2-each-through-Hydro price and now requires Road plus Hydraulic Assembly, adding the second slot per map face. Road Channels 2 retains 130 each through Shiny and requires Road Channels 1 plus Ore Separation, adding the third slot. Both sides of placement count sending and receiving endpoints together. Reversal uses no new slot; saved excess pairs remain operational. Road speed remains one item per five seconds for every material.
- Expansion shows a persistent W1 sending Cart → Road pair → H receiving Cart route diagram, explicitly guides both real connections, and completes only when produced Wood arrives Home. Basics retains its buffer exercise with an explicitly practice-only Cart schematic loan; normal-game unlocks are unchanged by tutorials. Updated current catalog/docs and regenerated live research-consumption analysis for the additional research prices.

<a id="node-0211"></a>
### NODE-0211 · Check Research Center Cores immediately on project selection

**2026-11-03 · Changed · Superseded · Local**

Selecting or resuming research immediately consumes one complete buffered Core set when the Research Center is ready, credits project progress and starts the successful-check glow.

- Later payments retain the five-second base interval and all six research-speed ranks. A saved payment deadline prevents same-project clicks, cancellation, switching and save/load from bypassing that interval.
- An incomplete set consumes nothing and starts no glow. Existing waiting-for-material behavior remains after an unsuccessful initial check. Disabled, processing-paused, unfinished or locked-sector Centers do not charge on selection.
- Existing contributions are restored before checking. Only still-required Core types are consumed, so an immediately successful final payment can complete a resumed project. Unavailable project requests preserve current processing and feedback.
- Extends NODE-0159 with an immediate initial check while retaining its interval baseline; successful payments use the glow added in NODE-0207.

Topics: Research · Simulation · Testing · Persistence

Replaced by: [NODE-0413](<2026-11.md#node-0413>)

Verification: Full Vitest suite: 583 passed, 1 existing skip. TypeScript/Vite production build passed. Added immediate-payment, atomic missing-input, ineligible-center, cooldown-through-switch/cancel/save/load, resumed-final-payment and invalid-selection regressions; checked exact subsequent payment boundaries at every speed rank and updated the resumed-project UI expectation. Changelog generation and checks passed. No browser or balance run for this simulation change; no publication.

### NODE-0207 · Pulse Research Centers between successful Core payments

**2026-11-03 · Changed · Implemented · Local**

- Timing follows simulation time across global pauses and save/load. Reduced-motion mode uses a steady soft highlight during the same window.

<a id="node-0140"></a>
### NODE-0140 · Add a universal Dev Source that automatically supplies connected inputs

**2026-11-02 · Added · Superseded · Local**

Dev tools can place a movable Dev Source with a multi-connection output that supplies each connected input with its required materials automatically.

- Available through Dev tools rather than the ordinary Build catalog. Placement, movement, deletion, save/load and undo use the existing node controls.
- Each semantic recipe socket gets its own material. A research CORE socket receives all outstanding required Core types. Bots, Stone, Forest Growth and any extant POWER input are inferred from the input family; deferred Power equipment stays deferred.
- An unconfigured production node may be wired to a Dev Source but receives nothing until its recipe is chosen. Recipe changes preserve valid Dev Source cables and update supplied materials.
- Extractors mine a virtual infinite reserve on their normal cycle, inferred from downstream demand. Lake Intakes accept a Dev Source upstream. Generic input families infer demand through local logistics or use an existing material, then Iron as fallback.
- Input buffers respect capacity and pending physical deliveries; cosmetic pulses do not create physical stock. Production time, research prerequisites, camp effects and visible obstruction boundaries remain in force. Ordinary sources keep their compatibility checks.
- Development QA only: these grants are not evidence about normal balance or progression. The live player game was preserved.
- NODE-0433 replaces direct Dev Source connections to sending Roads. Other Dev Source inputs retain their behavior.

Topics: Controls · Interface · Production · Research · Connections · Playtesting

### NODE-0127 · Use visible obstruction borders and reserve maximum camp growth on spawn

**2026-11-02 · Fixed · Implemented · Local**

Lakes, Deep Holes, camps and Golems share their drawn outline with placement, cable blocking and camp encroachment. Generation validates maximum camp size and reserves its full maximum radius from resources.

- Camp placement validates its 100% visible body against field edges and other obstructions before starting at 25%. Resources reserve the entire maximum circle plus their full body and ordinary placement clearance.

- Generation rules apply to newly generated sectors. Existing saved layouts are preserved.
